title: Do You Know a Leader Who Is Sleep Deprived?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This short piece treats chronic sleep loss in leaders as a brain-health problem rather than a badge of toughness. It explains that sleep clears waste from the brain, so a sleep-deprived brain tries to do that cleaning while awake and produces fog, poor focus and slow reactions. The author dismisses the claim that some leaders thrive on a couple of hours, saying the research does not support it. The recommended move is to seek professional help and avoid sleep aids that distort normal sleep, then enjoy better memory, alertness and immune function. The closing call is to encourage any sleep-deprived colleague to get help.
points: Sleep loss is framed as a medical brain issue to be treated, not a macho trait to tough out.
Deep sleep early in the night matters most, yet sleep-deprived leaders rarely get it.
The claim that some people function fine on very little sleep is rejected; individual tolerance varies but everyone suffers effects.
Professional guidance is preferred over sleeping aids, which can distort normal sleep architecture.
Leaders can help by nudging struggling colleagues toward help.
quotes: As we sleep at night, a fluid that surrounds the brain flushes out toxins and dead cells that build up during the day. This cleansing process keeps the brain working properly and helps to curb inflammation.

When people are sleep-deprived, the brain initiates this process while we are awake, causing all sorts of problems, including lapses in attention, an inability to focus, slower reactions, and a failure to pick up on auditory and visual cues. In other words, brain fog.

Despite the claim some leaders like to make that they don’t require much sleep and do fine on only a couple of hours, sleep studies prove that is hogwash. While some people can handle disrupted or less sleep better than others, everyone who is sleep-deprived experiences negative effects.

Smart leaders with a sleep problem treat sleep deprivation as a serious brain health issue, not something to “tough out.” They avoid relying on solutions that distort normal sleep architecture, such as sleeping aids, and consult experienced professionals to design an intervention that works.
Sleep is non-negotiable maintenance time for the brain. If any leader or team member you know is sleep-deprived, encourage them to seek the help they need.
